summary: In 1967 California high school teacher Ron Jones turned a lesson on Nazi Germany into the Third Wave, a five-day classroom movement with salutes, informants, show trials and enforcers that drew about 200 teenagers before he ended it.

evidence.note: Jones begins teaching in 1966 near San Francisco after Stanford; background on his style
experiment starts in the last quarter of his first year, in a sophomore world history class
class salute introduced; first dissenting student banished to the library
membership cards, secret informants and students reporting on each other
self-appointed armband bodyguards beat up students, likened to the SS
day five rally of about 200 members ends with a film of Nazi Germany and a lecture
hosts map the experiment onto Paxton's passions and Eco's traits of fascism
legacy: German school curriculum, films, documentary, Jones later fired and career since

notes: Primary subject is the experiment, so roles are empty and Ron Jones is secondary; his birth year 1941 is from general knowledge and his death status is unconfirmed (described as still teaching). Episode is hosted by Garrison Davis with Robert Evans as co-host. nazism kept as secondary because the whole simulation was modelled on Nazi Germany; fascism-far-right covers the Paxton/Eco analysis.
